title: SpiralPulse attention kernel + KV warmup optimizer (latency & throughput improvements)
author: Sofia Chen
description:
Summary: Introduces a new attention microkernel (SpiralPulse) that implements an alternating spiral tiling strategy for QK and fused rotary/rope application coupled with a lightweight KV warmup optimizer. The patch targets mid-long context workloads (1k-16k tokens) to reduce tail latency and improve sustained throughput under continuous batching.

Motivation: Existing tiled kernels favor uniform windowing which underperforms when prefix reuse and KV cache hot lanes dominate real traffic. SpiralPulse adapts tile ordering to maximize early warmup of hot KV lanes while allowing the hardware to stream unfused paths for cold lanes. Combined with a scheduler hint and a compact warmup heuristic, this reduces 95th and 99th percentile latencies while improving overall token throughput in production traces.

What I changed: single continuous description below -> Implements the SpiralPulse kernel in CUDA with a C++ wrapper, exposes a kernel selector that favors SpiralPulse for large context live-serving models, adds a KV warmup optimizer that tracks recent lane heat and prefetches KV into the L2-aligned slab before decoding begins, updates the continuous-batcher to emit warmup hints, and extends the runtime metrics to expose warmup hit rates and tile utilization. I also added unit tests and an integration benchmark harness used to collect the numbers in this PR.

Design notes: SpiralPulse alternates between inward and outward spiral tiling across the key dimension to prioritize local hot lanes. The kernel fuses rotary/rope application with the q/k projection to reduce memory traffic and uses half-accumulation when safe (FP16) to leverage tensor cores. The KV warmup optimizer is a low-overhead LRU-ish detector that promotes lanes to a warm queue when they exceed a usage threshold within a short window; warm lanes get preallocated contiguous KV slots and are populated via async memcpy before the first generation token. The overall approach keeps the hot path tight and falls back to the legacy kernel for small contexts or when mem pressure is high.

Benchmarks (representative):
- Production trace (conversational, mixed lengths 256-4096) on p4d-like instance: p95 token-latency down 18% (from 42ms to 34.5ms), p99 down 22%, throughput up 12% at 90th percentile concurrency.
- Long-context synthetic (12k sequence): end-to-end throughput +28%, per-step latency median unchanged, p99 improved by 16%.
- Memory impact: average device memory for KV increased by ~3% due to warm queue reservation (configurable), observed negligible impact on tail OOMs in normal workloads.

Compatibility and toggles: SpiralPulse is opt-in via a model runtime flag ("attn.kernel=spiral_pulse") and the KV warmup optimizer is controlled by a runtime knob ("kv.warmup.enabled"). Both default off for older deployments and enabled for the new Dedicated capacity fleet after staged rollout. The kernel selector falls back automatically to the previous fused kernel when SpiralPulse is not compatible.

Checklist: 
- [x] Kernel implementation (CUDA) + wrapper
- [x] Scheduler hints + continuous-batcher integration
- [x] KV warmup optimizer + config knobs
- [x] Metrics + dashboards (temp)
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Benchmarks and regression tests
- [x] Docs snippet for runtime flags

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the warmup heuristic conservative; aggressive policies increased throughput but caused memory fragmentation in some edge cases (recorded in the benchmark log). Follow-ups planned: more aggressive warm-to-cold demotion, per-model heat calibration, and experiments with alternate spiral stride factors.

Related: ENG-3421 (attn scheduling), ENG-3599 (kv cache improvements).

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Nice approach. Can you quantify the warmup optimizer CPU overhead under high QPS? The first benchmark run showed a slight CPU increase on the scheduler host.

Sofia Chen (author): The warmup path uses a single background thread and the detector is bounded; microbenchmarks show <2% CPU increase at 5k rps. I've added measurements to the bench harness and noted them in the docs.
Maya Lopez: Tests look good. Please add a safety gate so the warmup allocator is disabled when device free memory < 10%.
Sofia Chen (author): Added the safety gate and a unit test for low-memory behavior.
Kai Nguyen: CI had an intermittent failure in bench/latency_test on the first run; re-ran and it's green. Approving pending a small comment about a log message.
Sofia Chen (author): Fixed the log message and squashed commits per request.
release_notes: Introduce SpiralPulse attention microkernel and optional KV warmup optimizer. Expect lower p95/p99 latencies for medium-long contexts and improved throughput for sustained continuous-batching workloads. Flags: attn.kernel=spiral_pulse, kv.warmup.enabled (off by default).
